title: Tz-L-M
hook: tzelem, image, as in the image of God

segments.voice: Yesterday, K-B-D: honor as weight, and Moses' tired hands held up on the hill. Today, a root about faces.

Rush hour. A train car packed shoulder to shoulder. A man asleep against the window, mouth open. A teenager with headphones and a scowl. A woman doing her makeup in her phone's camera. Someone humming, someone crying quietly behind sunglasses. Nobody looks at anybody. The first chapter of Genesis makes a claim about every one of those faces, in one short word. Tzadi, lamed, mem: Tz-L-M. Tzelem. Image.
screen: `A PACKED TRAIN CAR.` → `NOBODY LOOKS AT ANYBODY.` → `TZ-L-M: IMAGE.`

segments.voice: You met this verse on day twenty-four; today, the word inside it. First: "And God created man in His own image, in the image of God created He him; male and female created He them." Tzelem, twice, and then a line so nobody misses who's included: male and female. Second, what the word names elsewhere. In other books, tzelem can mean a statue, like the images of Baal that the people of the land break in pieces in the book of Kings. A tzelem stands for someone. So Genesis takes a word for a carved figure and uses it for a person made of dust and breath. Third, the coins. The Mishnah, in tractate Sanhedrin, says: a human king stamps many coins with one seal, and they all come out alike. God stamped every person with the seal of the first human, and not one is like another. Fourth, what follows. After the flood, God tells Noah that whoever sheds a person's blood will answer for it, "for in the image of God made He man." Harm a person, and you've struck at the image. Rabbi Akiva, in Pirkei Avot, adds a softer line: a human is beloved, created in the image, and more beloved still that it was made known to him. Back to the train car. Genesis doesn't say those faces are nice, or right, or easy to sit next to. It says each one carries the image.
screen: `IN THE IMAGE OF GOD CREATED HE HIM.` · `A TZELEM: A FIGURE THAT STANDS FOR.` · `ONE SEAL, AND NO TWO ALIKE.` · `HARM A PERSON, STRIKE THE IMAGE.` · then, large: `צֶלֶם`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a face you passed recently without really seeing it: a stranger in a line, a driver, someone you find hard. Notice one thing about it that no other face has, a crease, a habit, the way they stand: one seal, and no two alike. Stay with that face for a few breaths, and if you pray, hold that person in the quiet.
Tz-L-M. Tzadi, lamed, mem: tzelem, image, the word Genesis uses for every human being made in the image of God. Today's word.
Your line: the image. Even the scowler by the window carries it. Rest well.

howItsDone: Jewish teaching draws on tzelem Elohim, the image of God in every person, when it speaks about human dignity; the Mishnah's teaching about one seal and no two faces alike is studied as part of tractate Sanhedrin.

chat.says: What does Genesis mean when it says people are made in God's image?
options: Each person carries the image, like coins from one seal, and yet no two are alike.
Genesis says it only of the first man, not of women or of the people after him.
It's only about faces; the Hebrew word tzelem simply means a face.
chat.meaning: Genesis says it of male and female alike, and repeats it after the flood. The Mishnah's coins: one seal, and not one person like another.

tzelem.meaning: Hebrew: image; elsewhere, a carved figure

Baal.meaning: a Canaanite god whose images were broken in Kings

Mishnah.meaning: the first great written collection of rabbinic law

Sanhedrin.meaning: the Mishnah tractate about courts, with the coins teaching

Akiva.meaning: a great sage of the Mishnah, quoted in Pirkei Avot
